title: Fix hand-rolled test _FakeMergeStore.remoteIsNewer implementations to match DriftMergeStore's clock-skew/D15 semantics

evidence.quote:
// Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics: strict `remote > local` outside
    // the ±5 s window; inside the window, server timestamp decides.

why: mergers_test.dart's fake claims to 'Mirror DriftMergeStore semantics' but omits the D15 fallback (drift_merge_store.dart:140-146): inside the clock-skew window with no decisive synced_at on both sides, the fake unconditionally prefers remote, whereas the real store first falls back to comparing raw updated_at (protecting a newer un-pushed local edit from being clobbered by an older remote). notification_settings_merger_round_trip_test.dart's fake is simpler still — no clock-skew window at all. Neither test currently uses timestamps close enough to trigger the divergent branch, so the suite passes today, but any future near-tie/clock-skew test added against these fakes would silently validate the WRONG (pre-D15) behavior, hiding exactly the bug class DriftMergeStoreTest exists to pin down.
recommendation: Replace both hand-rolled remoteIsNewer bodies with a delegate to the real DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (construct a throwaway DriftMergeStore over an in-memory DB inside the fake, or extract the pure comparison so both share one implementation) instead of re-deriving the algorithm by hand.
acceptance_criteria: A within-skew-window / no-syncedAt / older-remote test case added to either file fails before the fix and passes after, or the fake is proven identical to DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer by delegation (making such drift structurally impossible).
